correctness.rationale: The k-fold signed-vertex sum set is exactly {z in Z^5: ||z||_1<=k and ||z||_1 ≡ k mod 2}: constructive proof adds cancelling signed unit pairs after generating coordinate masses. Reflect to nonnegative orthant, write each y_i=floor(y_i)+fraction f_i, set integer slack t=k-sum floor(y_i), satisfying sum f_i<=t. Rounding up r largest fractions, for 0<=r<=min(5,t) with r≡t mod2, produces feasible sites with squared error E_r=sum f_i^2+r-2 sum_top_r f_i. Cases t=0,1,2 yield max squared error<=1 by explicit bounding E1 and min(E0,E2). For t>=4, Boolean parity-constrained rounding gives error<=5/4 (flipping minimum bias cost 2delta_min bounded by total squared-distance deficit), with all needed parity weights admissible. For t=3, if the full Boolean-parity minimizer is of forbidden weight5, optimality implies f_(4)+f_(5)>=1, and the split u∈[1/2,3/5] or [3/5,2/3] bounds admissible E3<=5/4; otherwise the minimizer itself is admissible. Explicit sites show equality: y=0 for k1, y=e1 for k2, half-integer five-vector for k>=3. Independently enumerated 12890 feasible quarter-grid cases and six full parity-lattice sharp witnesses; proof holds beyond finite tests.
